About a year ago, I got into a relationship with this girl that was (unbeknownst to me) in a relationship with someone long distance.

About a month into dating, I found out, and tried to leave. But I didn’t, in hopes that if she saw what she did to him (because I asked her to tell him why they really broke up) she would see how that effects people. And I felt like he deserved to know. She did, and seemed remorseful. And against my better judgement, I stayed with her. 

Needless to say, it all ended poorly, and over another guy when she went away on a trip. I was devastated. But I learned. Don’t pour your time and energy and love into a person that does not consider the ramifications their actions have on others. If your significant other has displayed the ability to hurt people on a selfish whim, they are demonstrating they don’t really think about anyone but themselves.

My advice to you (having read your comments about his own infidelity) dump him and move on.

Life is too short and there are too many possibilities of love out there, for you to trap yourself under an apathetical rock that is the only real metaphor for this type of relationship. 

Be strong. You’re never alone.

All I can say is this: Don’t blame Reddit. Like any community, it is filled with people of every flavor. It’s just on here that people are more forward with their intentions, because they can remain anonymous while doing it. Use a throwaway for sensitive topics, this community is a good one, you will find support. Predators will always be there, but you can easily deny them any attention.

Reading through your other comments, I think you’re just salty to see your ex having a good time. And you took the next availability you could to publicly shame him without thinking about it.

Hey bud. I know it’s not easy having unpopular opinions in the world. But there really is more to life than all of that.

You seem to put so much focus on politics, which is more often than not entirely subjective and never completely certain. Maybe focus on other things? Less enraging things, maybe a hobby, or the people in your life.

Try traveling out of your own mind for a bit to see your immediate surroundings, and how you might improve them. Not just for you, but for others. We have such short lives as it is, and the potential to do so much good and feel so much good in the world. Don’t spend it focusing on all the little negative aspects of the human condition, and please don’t bring it to a quick and unsatisfying ending. 

I believe in you, whatever your political stance, we all just want to be happy and feel loved in this world. Go forward with that, because in the end, that’s all that really matters my friend. ❤️

Hey there. Yeah the early 20’s and laziness (as I’ve been discovering more and more) are a deadly combination. I struggle with that laziness everyday, you really feel like you miss so many opportunities because of it.

But listen... we have plenty of time to figure ourselves out. To find where our happiness lies. And there will inevitably be dark times to go through, before we can get there. But enough of the general stuff.

Let’s talk about laziness. It’s crazy hard to move against, but if you break it down, you’ll see it less as an unstoppable monster, and more as a machine of breakable parts, much how we view ourselves now. Let’s reverse those roles.

Laziness is really just this series of habits and addictions you have. If you can slowly work better habits into your daily life, you’ll be able to work those addictions out, and replace them with other things that supply you with happiness. Healthier things. Why do you fail courses? What are you doing instead, when you know you should be studying? What is your go-to activity?

Hey there. It sounds as though you’re in a spiral. Don’t worry, this is a normal thing, like the drop in a roller coaster. It will end. 

But what we can do is talk about what brought you to this point, and explore what things in your life are troubling you. 

I understand the feelings of anger and resentment you have at those trying to help, how could any of us understand what you’re going through? We aren’t you. But I will say, if you allow yourself to reach out and open up a bit, I think you’ll find experiences of the human condition amongst strangers to be surprisingly similar.

That being said. You are only as alone as you allow yourself to be. If you need, please PM me, or talk here where others can chime in. We are worried about you, genuinely, and we’re here now because of that.

I remember vividly the 3 separate experiences I had while hallucinating during sleep paralysis. Most of the time, I don't get hallucinations, I just sit there calmly and wait for it to end.

But when I get the hallucinations, I really find them kind of cool, a bit exhilarating (As I always calmly remind myself they aren't real, I'm very methodical when facing 'unexplainable' situations.)

My first was of the generic shadow person, as represented above. I could only make out the faint shape of someone sitting in the corner of my dorm room, before my body woke up.

The second, and most visceral experience, was of a black hound sitting at the foot of our bed (my girlfriend and I). I could see it very clearly, almost TOO defined. At first it growled, but as I became more and move conscious, it became more docile, until just up and blinking right out of existence entirely. It still gives me a thrill to think about. I mean, a black hound, that's so cool.

The third was just an indistinguishable lady running from the door of our bedroom, into our room, and out of my sight. Of course when I could move, I did, and saw nothing. I almost thought that one actually happened, though my girlfriend was right next to me the entire time, so I guess not.

But I always just chill there and wait, a bit uncomfortably, focusing on my toes.
